obligation: DFARS cyber incident report affecting covered defense information
trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident that affects a covered contractor information system or the covered defense information in it (for example a tampered device connected in the FSCE configuration lab, or a compromise of the FSCE)
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery ("rapidly report")
notify: DoD through DIBNet (requires a DoD-approved medium assurance certificate); subcontractors also report to the prime
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - FSCE and any system that held CUI. Not triggered when only a supplier's own systems are compromised

obligation: Incident report number to the next higher-tier contractor
trigger: Company submits a DIBNet report on a subcontract
deadline: As soon as practicable after the DIBNet report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Federal Solutions subcontracts

obligation: Malicious software submission and media preservation
trigger: Malicious software isolated, or any cyber incident reported under 252.204-7012(c)
deadline: Submit malware to DoD Cyber Crime Center as instructed; preserve images and monitoring data for at least 90 days from the report
notify: DoD Cyber Crime Center (DC3); never the contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - FSCE

obligation: Covered telecommunications or video surveillance equipment discovered (Section 889)
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d)(1)-(2); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: The company identifies covered equipment or services used as a substantial or essential component of any system during contract performance, or is told of it by a subcontractor or other source
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further information within 10 business days of that report. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer (DoD contracts: through DIBNet); tell the prime the same day for subcontracts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - in all federal contracts and subcontracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: The company identifies a Kaspersky covered article provided to the Government or used during contract performance
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - where the contract includes FAR 52.204-23

obligation: FASCSA covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-30; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: The company identifies a covered article subject to a FASCSA order in a contract deliverable or in use
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the contract includes FAR 52.204-30; check each contract

obligation: Electronic parts from outside the authorized sourcing order, or not confirmed new
trigger: An electronic part for a DoD order came from a source other than the original manufacturer, its authorized suppliers, or a contractor-approved supplier, or cannot be confirmed as new and unused (including an unverified drop-ship substitution)
deadline: Promptly, in writing; keep inspection, testing, and authentication records for the Government on request
notify: Contracting officer (directly for prime contracts; through the prime for subcontracts)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - DoD contracts for electronic parts or end items containing them

obligation: Counterfeit or suspect counterfeit items (GIDEP)
trigger: Becoming aware or having reason to suspect that an item purchased for delivery to the Government is counterfeit or suspect counterfeit
deadline: Within 60 days: written notice to the contracting officer and a GIDEP report; keep the items until disposition instructions
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the clause is in the contract; check each DoD contract

obligation: Change in CMMC unique identifiers
trigger: A CMMC UID changes during the contract (for example a new assessment after a scope change)
deadline: During performance, as the change occurs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contracts with DFARS 252.204-7021

obligation: Cybersecurity incident decision (SEC definition)
trigger: Any severity-1 supplier or product event: decide whether it is an unauthorized occurrence on or conducted through the company's information systems (including resources it uses, such as the drop-ship portal and EDI)
deadline: At the disclosure committee's first meeting (within 48 hours of declaration under POL-03 4.4)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - publicly traded registrant

obligation: SEC materiality determination
trigger: A cybersecurity incident has occurred
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - publicly traded registrant

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
trigger: The disclosure committee determines the incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - publicly traded registrant

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: Disclosure would pose a substantial risk to national security or public safety
deadline: Only for the period the U.S. Attorney General determines and notifies to the SEC
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); SEC
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, if requested

obligation: SEC annual cybersecurity disclosure
trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the Form 10-K
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - describe lessons from the incident if relevant

obligation: Insider trading blackout
trigger: Severity-1 incident that may be material
deadline: Before the disclosure committee meets
notify: Committee members, responders with knowledge, executives
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy (not a regulation)

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state), for example reseller contacts or license registrants exposed through a compromised portal account
deadline: Varies by state (for example without unreasonable delay, or a fixed number of days)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside
clock_starts: Varies by state (often discovery or determination of the breach)

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above the state-set count of residents
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorney general or regulator where the state requires it
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check each state with affected residents

obligation: State consumer reporting agency notice
trigger: Breach above the state-set count of residents notified
deadline: Varies by state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check each state

obligation: State third-party agent (vendor) notice to the company
trigger: A vendor or agent that maintains personal information for the company has a breach
deadline: Varies by state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track inbound notices from suppliers, agencies, 3PLs

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach; 15 more days only on written good cause to the Department (individual notice only)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if company-held personal information of Florida residents is involved
clock_starts: Determination of the breach (or reason to believe a breach occurred)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (no extension)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (worked example)
trigger: A third-party agent determines a breach of personal information it maintains for the company
deadline: No later than 10 days after the agent determines the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - IT vendors have the term; staffing agencies and 3PLs do not yet (POAM-017)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Law enforcement report (voluntary)
trigger: Fraud, supplier impersonation, or criminal tampering
deadline: As soon as possible
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes (voluntary)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity (as defined in the final rule)
deadline: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment) - not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final

obligation: Cyber insurance notice
trigger: Suspected security incident, including supplier compromise and payment fraud
deadline: Per policy: call the carrier hotline before engaging incident vendors ($5 million retention)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Reseller and customer notices
citation: Reseller platform terms (SL-1); customer contracts; SOC 2 commitments
trigger: Affected products shipped to resellers or customers, or a platform incident affecting their data or availability
deadline: Per contract; product holds and serial lists as soon as affected shipments are known
notify: Affected resellers, integrators, and DoD customers (through Federal Solutions)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: OEM notice of suspect product in the authorized channel
trigger: Suspect counterfeit or tampered product bearing an OEM's brand, or a compromised authorized distributor account
deadline: Per agreement; promptly to keep authorization and warranty support
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual
